text:
anya: quick follow-up to iterator/transport discussions. main ask: don't leak transport or raw resume-token internals into public SDKs. we've had breakage from clients persisting internal cursors.

sam: agree. make resume tokens opaque and versioned. clients store a single string. server validates and accepts old formats for a migration window.

jin: ergonomics: per-language iterators that yield Page objects. Page -> items + bookmark + last_request_id. Python: generator/async generator. TS: AsyncIterable. Go: explicit Next()/Page(). keep surface consistent.

luis: retries: default iterator retries transient network/errors but expose RetryPolicy in client config and iterator-level overrides (with_retry / disable_retry). for non-idempotent endpoints require idempotency keys.

anya: prefetching: server may return optional prefetch_hint (avg_items, window_ms). SDK treats it as non-authoritative hint for local buffering only; never required for resume correctness.

sam: transport: discovery API advertises supported transports (paged-json, http2-stream, grpc). SDK auto-selects but allow override (transport_preference). iterator API stays identical across transports.

jin: backpressure: SDK maintains a small configurable page buffer (MaxBufferedPages). streaming transports must honor backpressure (window frames or token-bucket). for languages without native backpressure expose explicit buffer cap.

luis: throttling: on HTTP 429 / throttle frame iterator surfaces RetryAfterError with suggested wait. default behavior: wait & retry once; app can catch and decide.

anya: telemetry & migration: SDK logs a single warning when resuming deprecated bookmarks and emits telemetry for resume errors (invalid, expired, migrated). server accepts older bookmarks for N months and emits Deprecation header.

sam: cross-lang snippets: short examples for resume/patterns will go in RFC. also add note about storing bookmarks in ephemeral envs (serverless) and avoiding inline DB keys.

ci-bot: CI: unit=412, integration=27  all green.

anya: next steps: @jin will draft the follow-up RFC (bookmark contract, prefetch_hint schema, RetryPolicy knobs, discovery fields). @sam and @luis review. keep API thin and idiomatic per language. :thumbsup:
